page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top centre across the text column. Main text in one column on the left, with a narrow marginal note column on the right. Below the text: a catchword "Tan-" at the lower right, and a signature "R 4" at the lower left.

main_text.p: Gummi eft Lacryma aquofa ; Refi-na vero Oleofa & flagrabilis.
Calidæ, Temperatæ vel Intemperatæ, Temperatæ, ut : Cancamum feu Lac-ca, gummi Elemi, Tragacanthum, &c.
Intemperatæ, & quidem calidæ in primo Gradu ; Bdellium, gummi Hedera, Secundo ; Maftyx, Myrrha, Galbanum, Thus, Pix, Refina, Styrax. Tertio ; Ammoniacum, Cedri liquor, Quarto ; Benzoi, Euforbium.
Frigidæ funt : Camphora, gummi Arabicum, &c. De Camphora tamen dubitari poteft, aliquis enim gradus caloris in ea effe videtur.

Inter Gummi nonnulla etiam fecunda qualitate alterant, ut ; gummi Amygdalarū, Tragacanthum, Manna thuris, Sandaracha, Sarcocolla, Et hæc quidé adstringunt. Molliunt : Colophonia, Styrax, &c. Calculos pellit : gummi Ceraforum. Menses ciet Styrax.
Inter purgantia & quidem Pituitam funt : Sagapenum sive Serapinum, Sarcocolla, Opoponax, &c.

page.notes: Marginal note at right, top: "De Gummi & Refinu," (the printed text reads "De Gummi & Refinu,"). Printed in small italic type, so it is a note, not a heading; it is written as a foot paragraph above, which is a placement choice, not a text change. The lower-left running text ends with "Tan-" as the catchword; the next page opens with the rest of the word. Some faint show-through from the reverse side is visible in the right margin and centre and is not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "Serapinum" and "Sagapenum" are read as printed; "Arabicum" is read as printed. Word "Cancamum" is read as printed.
